# iliad-044 (7.283–378) — reviewer's record

Two passes over `units.json` (53 units). `t` was not touched (checked unit by unit against the original and against `source/iliad-monro-allen1920.json`; the joined `t` still reproduces lines 283–378). `gloss.json` was not touched and not read for content; the points that matter for gloss pass 2 are at the end.

Severity: **major** = a false statement in a note or a house-table rule broken in the English; **moderate** = a departure from English already shipped for the same Greek or formula, or a note that quotes what is not in the line; **minor** = precision or polish.

Totals: major 4 findings (5 unit edits), moderate 5, minor 7; 16 findings in all.

Checks made, all clean after the edits below: line division of `l` equals that of `t` in every unit; no `\n` in `i`; typographic ’ only, no ASCII apostrophe, no double spaces; “ on the first unit of each of the six speeches (7.284, 288, 327, 348, 357, 368), ” on the last (7.286, 301, 341, 352, 363, 375), nothing in between; nested ‘ ’ inside Hector's speech closes as ’” (7.302); `mark` on the first unit of each speech and nowhere else; `p` on exactly the seven Monro and Allen paragraph starts (283, 287, 303, 313, 344, 354, 365); every `ln` is the line the unit starts on; every "ends at the ano teleia in the middle of line N" claim checked against the line; cross-references checked against the source (1.531 διέτμαγεν, 2.388 τελαμών, 1.466 ὤπτησάν, 7.276 Talthybius and Idaeus, 7.436 the wall, 3.245 oaths) and against the published English of 7.282 in iliad-043 (the speech of Idaeus closes there with ”; 7.283 opens Ajax's answer, so no speech runs over from the previous part; Priam's speech closes at 7.378 and iliad-045 begins a new paragraph). Whole-unit repeats (7.287, 7.308–310 first two lines, 7.319–320, 7.323–325, 7.326, 7.354–355, 7.365, 7.367) were compared with the published `l` and `i`: identical. The scanner was run on all 96 lines: every line fits; none is flagged by the packet, so no metrical sentence was added to any note. For the record only: 7.353 fits with a licence (ἵνα lengthened before μή, cost 2.6) and 7.355 with Ἀλέξανδρος lengthened before Ἑλένης (cost 3.0, the same line as 3.329).

## Findings considered and refused

- **7.298 θεῖον ἀγῶνα.** Kept as “the divine gathering” in both layers. ἀγών is “gathering” in the table (8.200), θεῖος “divine”; every alternative (“temples”, “contest”, “assembly of the gods”) decides what the Greek leaves open. The note already says the place is not stated and the sense of the line is uncertain; that is what the sole-source rule asks. μοι with εὐχόμεναι is rendered “for me”; it is a dative of interest and the Greek does not choose between that and “to me”, so no change.
- **7.329 ἐΰρροον.** Kept with the river (“fair-flowing Scamander”, as the table's ἐϋρρεῖος “fair-flowing”). The word order allows αἷμα, and the note says so; the choice is stated, not hidden.
- **7.336–337 ἄκριτον.** Only the `l` layer was changed (above). The `i` “undivided” and the note's mention of the other reading (“without sorting”) stay. The Odyssey's adverbial ἄκριτον “endlessly” is a different use and is not imported.
- **7.353 ἵνα μὴ ῥέξομεν.** “unless we do thus” / “unless we do this” kept. Purpose “so that we may not do thus” makes nonsense of the sentence, and a flagged-as-awkward note is the honest course; no neater reading was found from the grammar. No change to the note beyond what the drafter wrote. Recorded for the owner if a human wants to look: this is the one line of the part where the sense is imposed on the particles.
- **7.309 ἀάπτους.** “untouchable” in `l`, “irresistible” in `i`, with a note saying the meaning is unknown and these are two traditional guesses: this is exactly the shipped treatment of ἀάπτους (table row 11.502). Not changed.
- **7.318 ὄπτησάν.** The edition prints the unaugmented form here; 1.466 and odyssey-096 have ὤπτησάν. `t` is fixed. The English of the line equals the English of 1.466 in iliad-005 (“and roasted them very carefully and drew them all off”), the note says the augment is missing, so nothing to change.
- **7.314 ἱέρευσεν “sacrificed”.** The table's 6.174 row prefers “slaughtered” for a plain killing and says "sacrificed" is possible; here the dative ὑπερμενέϊ Κρονίωνι makes it a sacrifice, and iliad-011 (11.402, same clause) and odyssey-062 have “sacrificed”. Kept.
- **7.366 θεόφιν μήστωρ ἀτάλαντος.** The Odyssey ships two renderings (odyssey-010 “a counselor equal to the gods”, odyssey-013 “a counsellor to match the gods”). The draft's “a counsellor equal to the gods” follows odyssey-010 and the Iliad table's ἀτάλαντος “equal”. Kept; it is not listed in new-renderings but needs no row.
- **7.286 note “(elsewhere the verb is ‘lead’)”.** True of ἄρχω with a people (table 2.494, 5.200); not changed.
- **7.331, 339, 341 κυκλήσομεν, ποιήσομεν, ὀρύξομεν as “let us”.** Kept; they are read as proposals beside the short-vowel subjunctives κατακήομεν, χεύομεν, δείμομεν, and the note says so.
- **7.333 αὖτε not in `i`.** The faint “in turn / again” of ὅτ’ ἂν αὖτε νεώμεθα is in `l`, not in `i`; “when we go back” is the natural English and no force is lost.
- **7.299 “any man” for τις in `i`.** Acceptable in a purpose clause; `l` has “someone”.
- **7.308 “unharmed”.** ἀρτεμής is “unharmed” in published iliad-031 (the same line); the table's Odyssey row 13.43 “sound” is for a different context; no change.
- **7.321 “wide-ruling Agamemnon”, 7.322.** Agrees with the table's εὐρὺ κρείων.
- **7.337 note “the plan for the Achaean wall that is built later in this book”.** True (7.436–441), kept; it is a cross-reference, not a claim about the poem's wider habits.
- **Quotation marks.** No change needed; checked as listed above.

## Consequences for other files (not edited by the reviewer)

- `new-renderings.md` (drafter's file) is now out of step with `units.json`. Do not copy these rows into the table: **7.321 νώτοισιν … διηνεκέεσσι** (now the Odyssey's “chines” / “cuts of chine”, a reuse not a new row); **7.337 ἄκριτον** (now “unsorted” in `l`, “undivided” in `i`, as the existing ἄκριτος rows; reword the row or drop it); **7.347 τοῖσιν δ’ Ἀντήνωρ πεπνυμένος ἦρχ’ ἀγορεύειν** (`i` is now “was the first to speak among them”, the existing formula; drop the row). The opening statement of that file, "no departure from an Odyssey rendering", was untrue of 7.321 and 7.347 as drafted and is true now.
- For gloss pass 2 (gloss.json was not edited): ἄκριτον needs a `__broaden__` entry, since the Odyssey's entry is only the neuter adverb “endlessly” and here it is masc. acc. sg. “unsorted, undivided”; κέκλυτε / κέκλυτέ should read “reduplicated aor. imper.” (the existing entries do); Ἀντῆνορ is vocative with ο for ω; πινυτήν is “discernment”, not “prudence”; κελαινόν is “dark”; ἔφαθ’ is already in the glossary as impf. of ἔφατο; ὄπτησάν is the unaugmented form (= ὤπτησαν); ἐγρήγορθε is the perfect imperative of ἐγείρω (pf. ἐγρήγορα); τετρηχυῖα is perfect participle (root of τρηχύς); ἀάπτους is of unknown meaning.

## Gloss pass 2

`gloss.json` read against every line of `units.json`; 103 new entries and 18 `__broaden__` entries checked (each broadened entry starts with the existing root-glossary text whole; each new entry is under 230 characters, typographic ’ only, no line numbers). Changes (all in `gloss.json` unless named):

| Form | Severity | What was wrong | What was done |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἄκριτον | major | Entry gave only the unit's own reading, dropping the Odyssey's ἄκριτος entry (neuter adverb “endlessly”), and said “undivided, undistinguished” where `l` has “unsorted” | The Odyssey entry kept whole + “ · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with τύμβον: ’unsorted, undivided’”. It stays a top-level entry, not under `__broaden__`, because the form is not yet in `iliad-glossary.json` and `build_iliad.py` refuses a `__broaden__` key that is absent there |
| Ἀντῆνορ (key ἀντῆνορ) | major | Voc. sg. with no mention of the vowel | “with short ο for the nominative’s ω” |
| πινυτήν | major | “understanding, prudence”; “prudence” is reserved for πεπνυμένος and `l`/`i` say “discernment” | “discernment, good sense” |
| τετρηχυῖα | major | Lemma ταράσσω with “formation uncertain”; the note on 7.345 derives it from the root of τρηχύς | Lemma τετρήχω, “from the root of τρηχύς ’rough’”, perf. part. fem. nom. sg. |
| ὄπτησάν | minor | “(= ὤπτησαν)” only | “the unaugmented form of ὤπτησαν” |
| ἐγρήγορθε | minor | Already “perf. imper.”; tidied (ἐγρήγορα glossed) | glossed ’be awake’ |
| διακρίνῃ | minor | “short-vowel -ῃ”: the ending is the ordinary long -ῃ | label removed |
| παυσώμεσθα | minor | ending given as “-σθα” | “-μεσθα (= Attic -μεθα)” |
| ῥέξομεν | minor | read only as aor. subj.; ῥέξομεν is also the future, and ἵνα μή is awkward here | “aor. subj. … (or fut.), after ἵνα μή” |
| ἀγορεύσω | minor | future only | “(or aor. subj.)” |

Checked and left: κέκλυτέ (known, already “reduplicated aor. imper.”), κελαινόν (known, “dark, black”), ἀάπτους (known, “meaning unknown”); all other entries agree with the parse of the line.

`new-renderings.md` brought into line with `units.json`: rows for 7.321 and 7.347 removed (reuses of the Odyssey’s “chines” and the existing speech formula, now named in the opening paragraph); the 7.337 ἄκριτον row corrected to `l` “unsorted” / `i` “one undivided mound”; the opening claim now reads “no row below departs from an Odyssey rendering of the same word in the same use”, which is true.
